findings.failure_path: Add specs/new-round/evidence/payload.json containing arbitrary operational data plus a candidate_sha256 value of 64 lowercase hex characters. is_candidate_receipt accepts it solely from that field, added_evidence_paths converts it into an exclusion, and if it is the only change the bound diff becomes empty and the gate reports no reviewed-path change without evidence. The supplied tests only exercise JSON lacking candidate_sha256, so they false-green this exact bypass.
findings.smallest_fix: Stop treating candidate-controlled JSON shape as proof of a receipt. Derive exclusions from an independently authenticated controller manifest, or bind the pre-evidence commit/tree so receipts need no exclusion; add a regression case with arbitrary JSON containing a valid-looking candidate_sha256 and require it to remain bound.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: The claimed bind-every-tracked-path behavior is bypassable because candidate-controlled JSON can classify itself as an excluded receipt.
A pull request can land unreviewed JSON content under an evidence directory by adding any 64-character lowercase-hex candidate_sha256 field.
For an otherwise unchanged candidate containing only such a JSON file, the exclusion removes the sole changed path and the gate can return no-change successfully.
The tests cover scripts, binary data, and JSON without a binding field, but omit the decisive mutant: arbitrary JSON carrying a syntactically valid candidate_sha256.
The full-repository default and literal pathspec handling are otherwise compatible with the shown CLI behavior, but the weak receipt classification invalidates its fail-closed contract.
The workflow change accurately leaves merge queues unsupported and is reversible; rollout should remain blocked until the receipt-exclusion bypass is resolved or explicitly accepted.
Diagnostics for dirty trees and invalid succession are actionable, but this bypass is silent because it produces the legitimate no-change outcome.
The shared gate attempts to authenticate controller evidence using content supplied by the candidate itself; the diff explicitly leaves this trust-boundary bypass open.
